chunks: And the Messenger of Allah, peace be upon him and his family, said:
“Avert the prescribed punishments through doubts. There is no intercession, no guarantee, and no oath in a hadd case.”

key_terms.اِدْرَءُوا الْحُدُودَ: Ward off or avert the prescribed legal punishments
key_terms.بِالشُّبُهَاتِ: By means of doubts, ambiguities, or legal uncertainty
key_terms.شَفَاعَةَ: Intercession on behalf of someone in judgment
key_terms.فِي حَدٍّ: In a case involving a prescribed punishment
key_terms.يَمِينَ: Oath sworn in a legal context

ai.seo_question: What does the hadith mean by averting prescribed punishments through doubts?
ai.summary: This hadith establishes a legal principle in applying prescribed punishments: when there is doubt or ambiguity, the hadd punishment is to be averted. It also states that in hadd matters, intercession, surety, and oath do not function as means to alter the legal ruling.
